vBRIEFInfo.description: Auto-synthesized minimal plan for PAN-2286: bug(supervisor): watchdog self-heal structurally broken — pan restart --dashboard capped at 15s default health timeout while boot-to-listen takes 15-92s; child stderr discarded

plan.title: bug(supervisor): watchdog self-heal structurally broken — pan restart --dashboard capped at 15s default health timeout while boot-to-listen takes 15-92s; child stderr discarded
plan.author: overdeck/auto-start

narratives.Problem:
## Symptom

Every watchdog-triggered dashboard restart on 2026-07-03 (~12 attempts, 06:57Z–09:26Z) failed with `pan restart --dashboard exited 1` after a consistent ~16–18s, ending twice in `WATCHDOG GIVING UP — manual intervention required`. The self-healing path has likely **never succeeded** on a loaded machine:

```
[2026-07-03T06:57:31.080Z] watchdog spawned pan restart --dashboard (pid 3613204)
[2026-07-03T06:57:49.725Z] watchdog restart failed: pan restart --dashboard exited 1
[2026-07-03T07:04:50.101Z] watchdog spawned pan restart --dashboard (pid 3740027)
[2026-07-03T07:05:06.746Z] watchdog restart failed: pan restart --dashboard exited 1
[2026-07-03T07:07:00.827Z] WATCHDOG GIVING UP — manual intervention required: The operation was aborted due to timeout
...
[2026-07-03T09:26:53.456Z] WATCHDOG GIVING UP — manual intervention required: fetch failed
```

## Root cause (verified in source)

1. **The health wait defaults to 15 seconds, and the watchdog never overrides it.**
   - `src/supervisor/server.ts:99` spawns `pan restart --dashboard` with no `--health-timeout` flag.
   - `src/cli/commands/restart.ts:178-180` leaves `healthTimeoutMs` `undefined` when the flag is absent.
   - `src/lib/platform-lifecycle.ts:210`: `const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? 15_000;`
2. **Dashboard boot-to-listen alone takes 15–92s**, so the 15s health window expires before even a healthy boot can start listening. Boot-timing lines from dashboard.log this morning: `+17312ms`, `+15174ms`, `+91780ms`, `+15444ms` (all "HTTP server listening" — health passes only after that). The restart is therefore **structurally guaranteed to exit 1** under exactly the starved conditions that trigger the watchdog in the first place. The operator SOP already says restarts need `--health-timeout` ≥ 120s; the watchdog violates it.
3. **The failure reason is invisible**: `src/supervisor/server.ts:101` spawns the child with `stdio: 'ignore'`, so the child's stderr (`✗ [health] health check at ... did not pass within 15000ms`) is discarded. The supervisor log only ever shows the bare exit code.

A secondary confusion multiplier: the exit-1 happens AFTER the child has already SIGTERM'd and respawned the dashboard, so the dashboard often does come back seconds later — while the watchdog has already recorded a failed attempt toward its give-up budget (`maxRestarts`), and (pre-PAN-2219-fix conditions) keeps burning attempts until `gaveUp`.

## Fix

1. In `src/supervisor/server.ts` `spawnRestart()`, pass an explicit generous health timeout (e.g. `--health-timeout 120000`), or thread `watchdogConfig` through so it is configurable.
2. Capture the child's stdout/stderr (pipe to the supervisor `log()` on failure) instead of `stdio: 'ignore'` so the next failure is diagnosable from supervisor.log alone.
3. Test: unit test that the spawned argv includes the health-timeout flag, plus a watchdog test where restart succeeds when boot takes 60s (fake timers per repo rule).

## Relations

- Concrete mechanism behind part of #2253 (no recovery guardian / silent outage — the guardian exists but its remedy cannot succeed).
- Amplifies #1711 (event-loop stalls trigger the watchdog; the doomed restarts then add churn on an already-starved box).
- Evidence from the 2026-07-03 morning incident; starvation driver that morning was the PAN-2148 workspace container crash-loop/rebuild churn (see #1740).
